references.title: Main clubhouse and detached north pavilion
references.dateNote: Filename 20200819_181403; no EXIF capture timestamp in the public media record. The 2024 upload date is not the capture date.
references.subject: Course-facing main clubhouse on the left; detached pavilion/annex on the right.
observations: Red timber walls, red tiled/profiled main roof and white bargeboards/fascia.
The main building has a projecting glazed cross-gable: tall rectangular glazing below the eaves and triangular glazing up to its ridge, divided by white mullions.
A narrow white-framed side window is visible left of the glazed projection. The detached pavilion has its own gable, pale closed front screens/glazing and a timber deck railing.
limitations: Photograph is older than the June 2024 orthophoto. Hidden/rear elevations and current solar panels cannot be read here.
Pavilion use is not captioned. Pale front panels cannot reliably be distinguished as blinds, curtains or fixed infill. No dimension or colour calibration is implied.
references.inspection: Downloaded image visually inspected; observations are not image-search captions.

references.title: Range building, mat strip and gravel circulation
references.dateNote: PXL filename and public WordPress image_meta.created_timestamp=1748447434 agree on the date; upload 2025-06-10. Camera timezone is not separately supplied.
references.subject: Building immediately beside the driving-range hitting mats; not the main clubhouse.
observations: Red vertical timber siding; a red profiled/tile-effect gable roof; white fascia, gutter, corner trim and downpipe.
A broad central opening has a rolled-up grey cover. A white-framed glazed door and separate small window stand to its right.
Individual green mats and black ball trays line a raised pale concrete strip; the circulation surface is pinkish gravel. A low bench and K BYGG sign are visible.
limitations: People hide parts of the facade. Rear elevations, opening dimensions and interior function are not fully visible.
Do not turn the whole mat strip into a covered driving range: this photograph shows outdoor mats beside a separate building.

functionEvidence.finding: The clubhouse contains the club office and Café/Shop 19:e hålet; the official address is Storsandsvägen 30.
The café also operates the golf shop; this does not establish a separate restaurant building.

The club describes seven gravel camper pitches with electricity, nearby changing rooms/toilets/showers, and drinking water/waste facilities at the clubhouse and servicehouse; exact servicehouse footprint is unlabelled.
Kompassen, Fiskarfänget and Norrfällsvikens Camping/Stugby are nearby hospitality facilities, separately listed from the golf café.
